answer: Correlation is the tell. One controller driving N heads shares one scheduler, one clock, one habit of which peer to attest next. Payout flows only to submissions whose arrival times survive an independence test against the network, and the yarrow draw that picks which pairs to compare needs no new data, only timestamps already public. Detection sharpens as a farm grows: every added head is another chance to catch a shared rhythm, so cost per clone rises with the number of clones. Faking it takes N genuinely separate machines; the nectar of one head never pays for that voyage.
